summary: This note covers the women's football tournament at the 2016 Summer Olympics, held in Brazil from 3 to 19 August 2016 with 12 teams from six confederations. It lists the final standings, with Germany winning its first title ahead of Sweden and Canada, and Brazil finishing fourth. It also gives tournament statistics: 26 matches, 66 goals, total attendance of 635,885, Melanie Behringer as top scorer with 5 goals, and Sweden receiving the fair play award.
one_line: Overview of the 2016 Summer Olympics women's football tournament held in Brazil, won by Germany over Sweden.
key_facts: The 2016 Women's Olympic Football Tournament was hosted by Brazil.
The tournament was held from 3 to 19 August 2016.
Twelve teams from six confederations took part in the 2016 Women's Olympic Football Tournament.
The tournament used 7 venues in 6 host cities.
Germany won the 2016 Women's Olympic Football Tournament, its first title in the event.
Sweden were the runners-up in the 2016 Women's Olympic Football Tournament.
Canada finished third and Brazil finished fourth in the 2016 Women's Olympic Football Tournament.
A total of 26 matches were played, producing 66 goals (2.54 per match).
Total attendance at the 2016 Women's Olympic Football Tournament was 635,885, an average of 24,457 per match.
Melanie Behringer was the top scorer of the 2016 Women's Olympic Football Tournament with 5 goals.
Sweden won the fair play award at the 2016 Women's Olympic Football Tournament.
The tournament was preceded by the 2012 edition and followed by the 2020 edition.
